# lean-pkg llms

print the agent-oriented usage contract.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg llms [--short] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--short` | a compact contract (~40 lines) cut from the full one: PURPOSE, STANDING RULES and the first line of each subcommand; no flag details, schemas or examples |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `llms` | print the agent contract (`--json`: `{"ok": true, "text": ...}`). `--short`: a compact contract of about 40 lines cut from the full text by its section headers, never kept by hand: the title, the `PURPOSE` header and its first three lines, `STANDING RULES`, and the `SUBCOMMANDS` header with the first line of each subcommand (no flag continuations, examples, receipt schemas, event schema or exit codes); every line is a line of the full text; `--json` adds `"short": true` | `[--short]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `llms` (exit 0): `ok`, `text`

## Examples

Print the agent contract (standing rules, status transitions, every subcommand, receipt and event schemas, exit codes), the text llms.txt carries below its header.

```bash
lean-pkg llms
```

Sample output:

```text
lean-pkg llms.txt — agent contract for the Lean 4 package registry

PURPOSE
...
```

A compact contract of about 40 lines cut from the full text by its section headers (purpose, standing rules, the first line of each subcommand).

```bash
lean-pkg llms --short
```

The contract as JSON, an object whose `text` holds the full contract.

```bash
lean-pkg llms --json
```
